themes_detail.label: Unleashed Dogs Surge
themes_detail.summary: Unleashed dog complaints spiked to 5 THIS WEEK compared to a baseline average of 0.8 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 567% increase (z-score: 6.43)—signaling either a sudden enforcement gap, behavioral shift, or emerging pack problem in CD 402.
evidence: 5 unleashed dog complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.8 weekly baseline (567% spike, z-score 6.43)
Represents highest statistical anomaly in recent 311 data
Peak recency: complaint data from current week
reporting_angles: Interview residents in high-complaint blocks; map geographic hot spots within Sunnyside/Woodside
Contact NYPD K-9 unit and Parks Enforcement: what changed in patrols or enforcement this week?
Investigate whether new dog park or off-leash hours triggered unintended consequences

themes_detail.label: Mobile Food Vendor Complaints Jump
themes_detail.summary: Mobile food vendor complaints hit 3 THIS WEEK, a 500% spike from the 8-week average of 0.5 per week (z-score: 3.54), suggesting either illicit vendor proliferation, sanitation issues, or encroachment on residential/commercial areas.
evidence: 3 mobile food vendor complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.5 weekly baseline (500% increase, z-score 3.54)
Second most recent spike after unleashed dogs
Follows pattern of sudden, concentrated complaint clustering
reporting_angles: Which streets/blocks are seeing vendor activity; are these licensed vendors or unlicensed operators?
Contact Department of Health and Parks Enforcement: are there new enforcement sweeps or changes in licensing?
Interview local business owners and residents: what are the specific complaints (noise, blocking sidewalk, sanitation)?

themes_detail.label: Plumbing Failures Spike
themes_detail.summary: Plumbing complaints surged to 20 LAST WEEK, a 139% increase from the 8-week baseline of 8.4 per week (z-score: 3.63), pointing to potential water system degradation, aging building stock issues, or localized infrastructure failure in CD 402.
evidence: 20 plumbing complaints LAST WEEK vs. 8.4 weekly baseline (139% spike, z-score 3.63)
Combined with 762 heat/hot water complaints over 90-day period, suggests housing/building infrastructure stress
665 building alteration permits filed in last 90 days may indicate aging stock in crisis
reporting_angles: Geographic clustering: are complaints concentrated in specific blocks or building types (prewar, post-war)?
Interview DEP about water pressure issues, mains breaks, or service disruptions in past 1-2 weeks
Human interest: interview tenants in affected buildings about repair timelines and landlord responsiveness

themes_detail.label: Overgrown Trees and Dead Animals
themes_detail.summary: Overgrown tree/branch complaints hit 6 LAST WEEK (243% spike from 1.8 baseline, z-score 5.13) and dead animal complaints reached 5 LAST WEEK (264% spike from 1.4 baseline, z-score 4.23), together suggesting environmental neglect, pest infestation, or deferred maintenance across the district.
evidence: 6 overgrown tree complaints LAST WEEK vs. 1.8 weekly baseline (243% spike, z-score 5.13)
5 dead animal complaints LAST WEEK vs. 1.4 weekly baseline (264% spike, z-score 4.23)
Both spikes clustered in same week, suggesting concurrent environmental stressor
reporting_angles: Contact Parks Department: why did tree maintenance fail last week; are there staffing or budget constraints?
Interview Parks or Sanitation about dead animal removal response times and underlying causes (disease, rodent outbreak?)
Map complaint locations: are overgrown trees blocking sightlines in high-crime areas or near schools?

themes_detail.label: Housing Code Violations Uptick
themes_detail.summary: Door/window complaints spiked to 15 THREE WEEKS AGO (140% above 6.2 baseline, z-score 3.67), and 665 building alteration permits filed in the last 90 days indicate widespread housing stock stress; combined with heat/hot water complaints (762 total), this signals systemic landlord compliance and maintenance gaps.
evidence: 15 door/window complaints THREE WEEKS AGO vs. 6.2 weekly baseline (140% spike, z-score 3.67)
762 heat/hot water complaints over 90 days (chronic, unresolved issue)
665 DOB building permits (476 alterations) suggest widespread renovation activity or code remediation pressure
reporting_angles: Investigate repeat offenders: which landlords/buildings account for multiple complaints across door/window, heat, plumbing?
Obtain DOB enforcement data: how many violations issued, how many resolved, penalty amounts?
Profile tenant experience: interview residents about repair request timelines and retaliation concerns
Context: tie to CB budget priorities (repeatedly requesting study of zoning and land use to match current needs)
